title: Score films for next year
prompt: The catalogue team wants to know which films will keep a high rating. Write `solve(ratings)` so it trains a model on how films did in 2025 and 2026, then scores every film rated in 2026 from its 2026 ratings.
rules: A film's feature is its average `rating` over the period. Ratings before 2026-01-01 are 2025; ratings from 2026-01-01 on are 2026.
Train on films rated in both periods: the feature is the 2025 average, and the label is 1.0 when the 2026 average is 4.0 or more, else 0.0. Use `LogisticRegression` with its default settings.
Score every film that has a 2026 rating, using its 2026 average as the feature.
Return `movie_id`, `prediction` and `p_high`, the probability of 1.0 rounded to 2 decimal places.
hints: One `groupBy("movie_id")` can give both averages: `F.avg` of a `F.when(...)` that is NULL outside the period skips the other period's ratings.
Training and scoring rows need the same feature column name, so the pipeline's `VectorAssembler` finds it in both. Fit the `Pipeline` on the training rows, then `transform` the scoring rows.
